syntax.syntax_item: R = tessera.fbm(sz, 'octaves', o, 'frequency', f, 'lacunarity', l, 'gain', g, 'seed', s, 'seamless', tf)

param_input_item.param_description: Field size: a scalar for a square field, or a [rows cols] vector.
Number of octaves summed (default 5). More octaves add finer detail.
Seed of the pseudo-random generator (default 0). The same seed reproduces the same field.
If true, sample each octave on a periodic lattice (default false).

param_output_item.param_description: The generated field, a rows-by-cols double matrix normalized to [0, 1].

description.p: Sum several octaves of Perlin noise into a self-similar fractal field. This is the workhorse of procedural terrain and cloud generation. frequency, lacunarity and gain control the spectral distribution; with 'seamless' true, each octave is sampled periodically for tileable output. The result is normalized to [0, 1].

xmldoc.bibliography: M. Hendrikx, S. Meijer, J. van der Velden, A. Iosup, Procedural Content Generation for Games: A Survey, ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications and Applications 9(1), 2013. DOI 10.1145/2422956.2422957.

example_item.example_item_data: R = tessera.fbm(256, 6, 1); imagesc(R); axis image off; colormap(tessera.colormap('terrain'))
